part_title: Customer Engagement: Amazon Lex, Amazon Connect and Human Handoff

scenes.title: Amazon Lex and Amazon Connect
scenes.narration: This final diagram follows a customer interaction from chat or voice into Amazon Connect, then to an Amazon Lex conversational bot. Connect manages contact flows and routing, while Lex interprets a user's intent, collects required slot values and manages the conversation state. When the dialog requires a business operation or grounded AI answer, a Lambda function or an approved Bedrock integration can call business APIs, knowledge sources or models. The lower branch shows an important outcome: when automation cannot confidently or safely resolve a request, Connect transfers the conversation to a human agent. Carry forward the authorised context and a concise summary so the customer doesn't have to repeat everything. That handoff must avoid exposing sensitive information beyond the agent's permissions. For example, a billing assistant can identify the account issue, retrieve allowed status data, answer common questions and escalate a disputed charge to a specialist. Lex isn't itself a contact-center platform, and Connect isn't a replacement for application authentication or Bedrock safeguards. Use the two together to blend efficient automation with supervised human support.
